stance_rationale: Reject as approvable alpha evidence: the reported multi-horizon signal is selected with full-lockbox ICIR weights and then evaluated on the same history, while the authoritative portfolio-alpha t is far below the 2.95 hard hurdle. It can be logged only as a failed/scoped hypothesis after a walk-forward rebuild and contract cleanup.

time_series_alpha_audit.comment: The artifact is multi-date, so RF-A7 single-snapshot alpha is not triggered. However it uses column alpha rather than score_*, and the blend weights are a single lockbox-wide ICIR fit rather than a PIT rolling/expanding schedule.

pit_c1_c15_audit.evidence: mh_alpha_build.R uses Z_Score_Aligned via load_month_factors(); no NEGATE_FACTORS or manual sign flip found.
Horizon blend weights are ICIR-proportional using the whole <=2023-12-22 IC history, so early sig_dates use IC evidence not usable at those sig_dates.
Factor inputs are loaded through load_month_factors(sd), not direct monthly factor parquet reads.
No regime/DD/vol overlay enters the alpha score construction.
Fundamental lag handling is delegated to Factor DB aligned Z_Score_Aligned fields; package declares quarterly 45d and annual May rules.

critical_concerns.description: The central claim that the blend beats the best single horizon is learned from full-lockbox ICIR weights and evaluated on the same dates. This is a process-level future-information problem for the weight schedule; the 0.382 vs 0.360 ICIR edge is not valid until rebuilt with rolling or expanding weights available strictly before each sig_date.

Authoritative canonical portfolio-alpha t is 0.73686 full and 1.317753 lockbox, both far below the 2.95 hard hurdle. The same canonical screen reports turnover 9.73-9.92x/year, above the base hard turnover cap of 6x/year, and uses top-25 while the base mandate says max_names=20 hard.

AX-007 is not actually satisfied: the handoff is one scalar BLEND_ic score feeding a long-only top-25 screen, with MID assigned zero weight. Calling the construction multi-sleeve does not make the portfolio a genuine multi-sleeve allocation, long-short book, 50+ name diversified book, or ML sizing exception.

Requested triangulation artifacts are absent or path-mismatched: qepm/stage_artifacts/WT_WT-D20260529_005 is missing, stage_artifacts/WT_D20260529_005 is missing, weights.csv is missing, covariance.parquet is missing, and risk/optimization packages are missing. The present challenge_note.md addresses CAP_TIER, not the primary MULTI_HORIZON package.

RF-A4 is unresolved for the primary package: no sector-neutral ICIR drop test is reported for MULTI_HORIZON. RF-A5 is also not perfectly clean: top-decile scores include about 1.46% names below 2e8 KRW ADV and about 0.19% below 1e8 KRW ADV, so liquidity feasibility is not strictly hard-filtered at the alpha handoff level.

Core references are author-year only and lack concrete paper titles/pages. KR applicability is inferred mainly from the same backtest diagnostics, while the construction reuses value and quality proxies that sit near active KR failure patterns unless the AX-003/AX-004 exceptions are proven out-of-sample.

The package rationalizes high realized return correlation versus STR_1715 at 0.769883 as structurally unavoidable. Low signal correlation does not settle crowding/capacity risk when realized long-only returns remain highly correlated and beta/first-eigenmode exposure dominates.

supporting_arguments: RF-A3 nominally passes: recent36 ICIR 0.504065 is about 1.32x lockbox ICIR 0.382158, below the 1.5 threshold.
RF-A7 single-date artifact is not triggered because alpha_scores.parquet has 267 monthly sig_dates and no Date/Ticker duplicates.
C13/C15 controls look sound for factor values: the implementation uses Z_Score_Aligned and load_month_factors().
The package honestly reports that portfolio-alpha t fails; the rejection is because the remaining signal-level claim and handoff contract are still not approval-grade.
unresolved_disputes: Whether BLEND_ic still beats SHORT when horizon weights are learned walk-forward using only IC history usable before each sig_date.
Whether the result survives a top-20 canonical screen with turnover <6x/year and a strict 2e8 KRW liquidity floor.
Whether MULTI_HORIZON has a sector-neutral RF-A4 robustness result comparable to the separate SECTOR_REL track.
Why the package uses a 2023-12-22 lockbox cutoff when the base context states lockbox sealed at 2024-01-23.
Whether missing weights.csv and covariance.parquet are intentionally downstream-only or a silent omission for this critique request.
weakest_assumption: The single weakest claim is that full-lockbox ICIR weights can validate a horizon-decay diversification edge on the same history used to choose those weights.
rebuttal_required: Rebuild MULTI_HORIZON alpha_scores with rolling or expanding horizon weights computed only from prior usable IC history at each sig_date.
Emit a clean alpha artifact with Date, Ticker, score or score_* and confidence; keep forward returns out of the handoff file.
Rerun RF-A1 through RF-A7 under the walk-forward artifact, including sector-neutral RF-A4 and best-single-factor/sleeve RF-A2 comparisons.
Rerun canonical_screen_bt with max_names=20, turnover cap <6x/year, 2e8 KRW liquidity floor, and report portfolio-alpha t plus DSR.
Provide a MULTI_HORIZON challenge_note.md, artifact_lineage.json, and explicit downstream status for weights.csv and covariance.parquet.
rationalization_red_flags: KR long-only realized return cor structurally high

verification_triangulation.additional_perspective: The package is useful as a negative research trace, but not as validated alpha evidence. The key external concern is not the reported rank-IC level; it is the non-PIT horizon-weight selection plus failure to translate into a hard-gate portfolio result.

alpha_specific_questions: Can this factor keep t_NW > 2.95 after the horizon weights are learned walk-forward rather than full-lockbox?
Does the alpha vector have future leakage through ICIR weight selection, especially for early sig_dates?
If AX-007 is invoked, where is the actual multi-sleeve allocation or other allowed exception rather than a single scalar top-25 screen?
